purpose: How patients get a medical cannabis card, state by state, from the regulator's own pages. Covers every medical-only state and, as they are reviewed, states where adults can also buy. Each fact names its source. A missing fact means the regulator page we checked did not state it; it does not mean the program lacks it.

states.agency: Florida Department of Health, Office of Medical Marijuana Use

who.text: Permanent or seasonal Florida residents diagnosed with a qualifying medical condition by a qualified physician.

items: See a qualified physician. The physician diagnoses a qualifying condition and enters you in the state’s Medical Marijuana Use Registry.
Apply for your registry ID card online or by mail.
Once approved, fill your physician’s order at a licensed medical marijuana treatment center, in person or by delivery.

card_length.text: Renew every year. Renewals open 45 days before the card expires.

caregivers.text: Allowed. Minor patients must name a caregiver, and every caregiver needs their own registry card.

visitors.text: Only permanent or seasonal Florida residents can get a Florida card.

buy.text: Only at state-approved medical marijuana treatment centers, which may also deliver.

states.agency: Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority

who.text: Oklahoma residents with a physician recommendation form signed within 30 days of applying.

items: Have a physician complete the patient recommendation form.
Apply online with OMMA, with proof of identity, proof of Oklahoma residency and a photo.
Buy from any licensed dispensary with your patient license.

fee.text: $100 (plus a $4.30 card-processing fee). $20 for patients on Medicaid/SoonerSelect or Medicare and for 100% disabled veterans.

card_length.text: Two years, or 60 days for a short-term license.

caregivers.text: Allowed, with no application fee. A patient can have one caregiver at a time, and the physician must certify the need for one.

visitors.text: Patients with a state-issued card from another state can get a 30-day temporary Oklahoma license ($100) to buy, use and grow.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. Show your patient license every time you buy.

fee_help.text: $20 instead of $100 with proof of Medicaid (SoonerSelect) or Medicare enrollment, or 100% disabled veteran status.

states.agency: Mississippi State Department of Health, Medical Cannabis Program

who.text: Patients with a qualifying condition, certified after an in-person visit by a registered practitioner: a physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner or optometrist. Only a physician (MD/DO) may certify a minor.

items: Get certified at an in-person visit with a practitioner registered with the Department of Health. Renewal check-ups may be by telehealth.
Apply in the Department of Health’s licensing portal. Review takes about 10 days once the application is complete.
Buy at a licensed dispensary with your registry card.

fee.text: $25 ($15 for Medicaid participants). Disabled veterans and disabled first responders with documentation can have the fee waived.

card_length.text: The certification is good for one year unless the practitioner sets a shorter time.

caregivers.text: Allowed. A minor’s caregiver must be the custodial parent or legal guardian.

visitors.text: Nonresident cardholders can buy, with lower limits: six MMCEUs a week and twelve in any 15 days.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. The Mississippi Department of Revenue permits dispensaries; the Department of Health licenses the rest of the program.

fee_help.text: $15 instead of $25 for Medicaid participants. Waived for disabled veterans and disabled first responders with documentation.

states.agency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services, Center for Medical Cannabis

who.text: Utah residents 18 or older with an approved medical condition.

items: Create a Utah ID and an account in the state’s electronic verification system (EVS).
Meet in person with a medical provider, who submits your certification in the EVS.
Pay the card fee when the emailed instructions arrive.
Meet with a medical cannabis pharmacist before your first purchase, in person or by phone or video.

card_length.text: One year, unless your provider sets a shorter time.

caregivers.text: Caregiver cards and minor patient/guardian cards are available.

visitors.text: Visiting patients with a home-state card for a listed condition can get a non-Utah resident card. It lasts 21 days, with up to two a year.

buy.text: Licensed medical cannabis pharmacies or home delivery.

states.agency: West Virginia Office of Medical Cannabis

who.text: West Virginia residents with a serious medical condition, certified by a registered physician.

items: Get certified by a registered physician, in person or through a listed telehealth company.
Register in the online portal and pay the fee. Applications are reviewed within 30 days.
Download your digital card and buy at a licensed dispensary.

fee.text: $50. The fee can be waived for income below 200% of the federal poverty level.

card_length.text: Renew every year after a visit with a registered physician.

caregivers.text: Up to two per patient. Patients under 18 must have one.

visitors.text: The program is for West Virginia residents, and cardholders may not take medical cannabis out of the state.

buy.text: Dispensaries licensed by the Office of Medical Cannabis.

fee_help.text: The $50 fee can be waived for household income below 200% of the federal poverty level.

states.agency: Alabama Medical Cannabis Commission

who.text: Patients 19 or older with a qualifying condition, recommended by a physician certified by the Alabama Board of Medical Examiners and registered with the Commission. Caregivers register to obtain it for minors.

items: See a registered certifying physician.
Register with the Commission through its online portal.
Only registered patients and caregivers with a valid Alabama card may enter a dispensary.

caregivers.text: Allowed. Parents and others can register as caregivers for minors.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. The first opened on June 4, 2026, and the Commission posts openings on its patients page.

note.text: Dispensaries are still opening. Check the Commission’s patients page for current locations.

states.agency: Arkansas Department of Health

items: Apply online with the Department of Health’s medical marijuana registry.
Processing can take up to 14 days. When approved, print your own card.

caregivers.text: Allowed. Caregivers pay $50 plus a $40 background-check fee.

visitors.text: Visiting patients apply online and pay $50 for 90 days. Ask the dispensary about its visiting-patient process.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage Control licenses them; the Medical Marijuana Commission lists locations.

states.agency: Hawaii Department of Health, Medical Cannabis Registry Program

who.text: Patients certified by a licensed Hawaii physician or advanced practice registered nurse for a recognized debilitating condition.

fee.text: State registration is $35 for a one-year certification or $105 for three years. Providers may charge up to three times that for the certification itself.

card_length.text: Certifications run one or three years.

visitors.text: Patients with a home-state card can register for up to 60 days, and renew once a calendar year for another 60.

buy.text: Licensed retail dispensaries regulated by the Department of Health.

states.agency: Kentucky Office of Medical Cannabis

who.text: Patients with a qualifying condition and a written certification from a medical cannabis practitioner.

items: Get a written certification from a medical cannabis practitioner (the state’s Find a Practitioner directory lists them).
Apply in the Patient and Caregiver Registry Portal with a notarized signature page and the fee.
Buy at an open licensed dispensary.

caregivers.text: Allowed. Patients under 18 may use medical cannabis only with a parent or legal guardian as their caregiver.

visitors.text: Visitors 21 or older with a valid out-of-state card and a documented qualifying condition can register for a Kentucky card.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. The Office has issued 48 dispensary licenses; it lists the ones that have opened.

note.text: Since July 1, 2026, Kentuckians who buy medical cannabis in another state no longer qualify for the governor’s conditional pardon.

states.agency: Louisiana Department of Health

who.text: Any patient with a valid recommendation from an authorized Louisiana clinician in good standing with their licensing board. No state agency keeps a list of recommending clinicians.

card_length.text: A recommendation expires no more than 12 months after it is issued.

buy.text: Licensed retailers: up to 10 base sites, each with up to two satellite locations. Raw flower is limited to 71 grams every 14 days, and retailers may not deliver outside Louisiana.

states.agency: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services, Therapeutic Cannabis Program

who.text: New Hampshire residents certified by a New Hampshire-licensed provider with prescribing authority.

items: Have your provider complete a written certification.
Mail or drop off the patient application, the certification, a $50 check or money order and proof of New Hampshire residency to the Therapeutic Cannabis Program, 29 Hazen Drive, Concord.

fee.text: $50. The program has no reduced fee for hardship.

card_length.text: A provider may certify a patient for up to three years.

caregivers.text: Caregivers must be 21 or older with no felony conviction. They get their own ID card and pay no fee.

visitors.text: Visiting patients can buy at a New Hampshire treatment center with their out-of-state card and matching photo ID, up to 2 ounces in any 10 days.

buy.text: Seven nonprofit alternative treatment centers, in Chichester, Conway, Dover, Keene, Lebanon, Merrimack and Plymouth.

states.agency: North Dakota Health and Human Services, Medical Marijuana Program

who.text: North Dakota residents with a written certification from a healthcare provider licensed in North Dakota. Veterans using VA care and hospice patients have a separate approval route.

items: Create an account in the state’s BioTrackTHC registration system.
Submit the patient application with a photo, a copy of your North Dakota ID, your provider’s name and email, and a signed release.
Buy only at one of the state’s eight registered dispensaries.

card_length.text: Renew up to 45 days before your card expires.

caregivers.text: Up to five per patient. Caregivers pass a criminal history check.

visitors.text: Visitors 19 or older with a home-state card can get a 60-day North Dakota card for $40.

buy.text: Eight registered dispensaries.

states.agency: South Dakota Department of Health, Medical Cannabis Program

who.text: Patients with a debilitating condition certified by a South Dakota-licensed physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse registered with the program.

items: Get certified by a registered practitioner.
Apply through the online registration system with your medical documentation and the fee.

buy.text: Certified dispensaries. The Department of Health publishes a list of certified establishments.

states.agency: Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission

note.text: The Commission licenses businesses, and its licensee list shows cultivators. When we checked, its site published no patient card process and no list of open dispensaries.

states.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Health

who.text: Pennsylvania residents with one of 23 serious medical conditions, certified by a practitioner approved by the Department.

items: Register online. You can do this before you see a practitioner.
See an approved practitioner, who certifies you in the system.
Pay for your ID card within 60 days of the certification. It is printed in about 7 days and mailed in about 14.
Visit a Pennsylvania dispensary with your ID card.

fee.text: $50. People in Medicaid, PACE/PACENET, CHIP, SNAP or WIC may qualify for a no-cost card.

caregivers.text: Allowed. Caregivers pass a background check, and minors get medical marijuana through a caregiver.

visitors.text: Registration requires a Pennsylvania driver’s license or state ID.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. The Department publishes a list of dispensaries with product.

fee_help.text: People in Medicaid, PACE/PACENET, CHIP, SNAP or WIC may qualify for a no-cost card instead of paying $50.

states.agency: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Cannabis Control

who.text: Patients with a qualifying condition, confirmed by a physician certified to recommend medical cannabis. The physician needs your Ohio driver’s license, Ohio ID card or another ID the Division approves.

items: Visit a physician certified to recommend medical cannabis, in person or by telemedicine. The State Medical Board’s search lists them.
The physician enters the recommendation and your profile into the Patient & Caregiver Registry. Ask them to mark indigent or veteran status if it applies.
Open the registry’s email (subject “ACTION NEEDED: Ohio MMCP Registry - Account Registration”), follow the link and activate your card.
Buy at a licensed dispensary with your active card, active recommendation and government-issued ID.
Renew each year after a visit with your physician.

fee_help.text: Indigent status (for example SSDI or SSI enrollment) and veteran status are recorded at registration. Send proof to the Division if your physician did not mark it.

card_length.text: Renew every year. A recommendation can cover up to a 90-day supply with three refills, 360 days in all.

caregivers.text: A registered caregiver may possess and administer medical cannabis for the patients listed on their registration. The recommending physician registers the caregiver.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. The Division publishes a map of them.

states.agency: New Jersey Cannabis Regulatory Commission, Medicinal Cannabis Program

who.text: Patients diagnosed with a qualifying condition by a New Jersey healthcare practitioner registered with the program, with whom they have a bona fide relationship.

items: Check whether your healthcare provider takes part in the program, or find a participating practitioner.
The practitioner diagnoses a qualifying condition and orders up to 85 grams for each 30-day period.
Enroll with the Medicinal Cannabis Program and get your ID card.
Fill the order at a state-licensed Alternative Treatment Center or dispensary.

fee.text: Digital ID cards are free. A physical card costs $10.

card_length.text: Two years. Renewal reminders go out 60 days before the card expires.

caregivers.text: Patients who cannot travel to a dispensary may designate and register caregivers to buy for them.

buy.text: State-licensed Alternative Treatment Centers and dispensaries.

states.agency: District of Columbia Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration (ABCA)

who.text: District residents of any age and non-residents 21 or older. Residents 21 and older can self-certify; residents 20 and younger need a healthcare practitioner’s recommendation, and minors need an adult caregiver.

items: Create an account in ABCA’s system and submit the registration.
District residents get a temporary digital registration right away, good for 90 days while staff review it.
A two-year digital registration follows a successful review.

fee.text: Free for District residents. Non-residents pay $10 to $100, depending on the period they choose.

card_length.text: Two years for District residents. Non-residents choose a period from 30 to 365 days.

caregivers.text: A caregiver can be affiliated with an adult or minor resident patient.

visitors.text: Non-residents 21 or older can register by self-certifying. Patients from jurisdictions with reciprocity can also use their home registration; ABCA lists the eligible jurisdictions.

buy.text: Licensed medical cannabis retailers. Registered patients can buy up to 8 ounces in a rolling 30 days.

states.agency: Washington State Department of Health

who.text: Any patient, regardless of age, whose healthcare practitioner authorizes cannabis as medically appropriate. Minors need a parent or legal guardian as their designated provider.

fee.text: At least $1 for the recognition card. Stores may charge more.

card_length.text: An authorization can be good for up to a year for an adult and up to six months for a minor.

caregivers.text: A designated provider 21 or older, with their own authorization form from the patient’s practitioner, can buy and grow for the patient.

buy.text: Medically endorsed retail stores. Patients with a recognition card pay no excise or sales tax on Department of Health medical products there, and may hold up to three times the recreational limits.

states.agency: New Mexico Department of Health, Medical Cannabis Program

items: Visit your medical provider. Only a medical provider can start an application, new or renewal.
Register or log in to the Online Patient Portal.
Complete the application online with your New Mexico ID or driver’s license. Your electronic card is available as soon as you are approved.

fee.text: None. The Department of Health charges no fee to enroll, take part or use the patient portal.

states.agency: Maryland Cannabis Administration

who.text: Anyone living in Maryland whose provider recommends medical cannabis for a qualifying medical condition.

items: Create an account at Maryland OneStop and verify your email.
Complete the patient application online, with your documents ready to upload.
After approval, you can order a patient ID card.

fee.text: $25 for the patient ID card, ordered after approval.

caregivers.text: A patient may name one caregiver aged 21 or older. Minor patients must have at least one caregiver who is a parent or guardian, and may have up to four.

buy.text: Licensed Maryland dispensaries.

states.agency: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services

who.text: Patients with a qualifying condition certified by an MD, DO or nurse practitioner licensed and in good standing in Missouri.

items: Have an MD, DO or nurse practitioner complete the Physician Certification Form.
Register in the department’s secure online registry portal and submit the patient application.
Renew in the window from 60 to 30 days before the card expires, with a new certification.

card_length.text: Three years for applications approved on or after December 8, 2022.

caregivers.text: Caregivers apply online with a Patient Authorization Form and the patient’s ID card number. A minor’s parent or legal guardian must apply as caregiver.

visitors.text: A person with an equivalent card or authorization from another state is not subject to arrest under Missouri law for possessing less than the limits set for Missouri patients.

buy.text: Licensed dispensaries. A patient may buy up to 6 ounces in 30 days unless certified for more.

states.agency: Virginia Cannabis Control Authority

who.text: Permanent or temporary Virginia residents, 18 or older or with a parent or guardian’s consent, with a valid government-issued ID and a condition a licensed practitioner finds may benefit.

items: Meet the basic qualifications.
See an eligible practitioner: a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse. If you are a good candidate, they issue a written certification.
Take the certification and your government-issued ID to a licensed dispensary, which scans the certification’s QR code.

card_length.text: The practitioner sets how long the written certification lasts, up to one year.

caregivers.text: The practitioner can add a registered agent to the certification for patients who need help. Parents or guardians can receive a certification for a minor or vulnerable adult.

buy.text: Licensed medical cannabis dispensaries.

states.agency: Vermont Cannabis Control Board, Medical Cannabis Program

who.text: Vermont residents with a debilitating medical condition, verified by a healthcare professional: a physician, osteopathic or naturopathic physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner.

fee.text: $50 with each initial or renewal application, non-refundable.

caregivers.text: A registered caregiver is a Vermont resident over 21 who can go to the dispensary, receive deliveries and help grow for up to two registered patients.

buy.text: Dispensaries. Medical patients pay no tax on their purchases.

states.agency: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Medical Marijuana Registry

who.text: Colorado residents 18 or older with a qualifying medical condition. Minors qualify with a Colorado-resident parent and two provider certifications.

items: See your health care provider, who submits a provider certification electronically. You need a new one each time you apply.
Complete your application online within 6 months of the certification, with your Colorado ID or driver’s license.
Complete applications are approved in 1 to 3 business days.
Print or display your card from your online account.

fee_help.text: The fee can be waived for household income at or below 185% of the federal poverty level, shown by a tax return.

states.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health, Medical Cannabis Patient Program

who.text: Illinois residents who meet the program requirements. The Department reviews applications and issues registry cards, which patients print or download from their online account.

fee_help.text: Veterans with an honorable or general discharge who are eligible for VA services get a reduced application fee, with a copy of their DD-214.

note.text: Veterans who get their care at a VA facility do not need a physician’s written certification. They submit their VA medical records for the last 12 months instead.

states.agency: Maine Office of Cannabis Policy, Medical Use of Cannabis Program

visitors.text: Visiting patients show their home state’s registry card or other state-issued patient document, if their home state allows it. They may buy up to 2.5 ounces every 15 days. The Office lists the approved states.

buy.text: Registered caregivers and medical dispensaries. Medical cannabis in Maine is not subject to mandatory contaminant testing or statewide inventory tracking.
